title: U.S. House · Louisiana's 1st District
area: Southeast Louisiana, including the New Orleans suburbs of Jefferson and St. Tammany parishes and the Northshore of Lake Pontchartrain.

context.text: Louisiana's 2026 U.S. House elections use a "majority vote" (all-party) system: every candidate, regardless of party, appears on one ballot on November 3, 2026 (Louisiana's filing deadline was August 7, 2026). If no candidate wins a majority, the top two finishers advance to a December 12, 2026 general election. The partisan primary and runoff originally scheduled for May and June 2026 were canceled after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Louisiana v. Callais that the state's congressional map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, requiring a new map.

candidates.name: Steve Scalise
candidates.currentRole: U.S. House Majority Leader (since 2023); U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 1st District (since 2008)

summary.text: Steve Scalise represents Louisiana's 1st Congressional District, stretching from the Northshore of Lake Pontchartrain to the New Orleans suburbs. First elected to Congress in 2008 after serving in the Louisiana State Legislature, he has served in House Republican leadership since 2014, including as Majority Whip, Minority Whip, and, since January 2023, House Majority Leader, the second-highest position in House Republican leadership.

background.text: Native of Jefferson Parish, Louisiana; graduated from Louisiana State University with a degree in computer science and a minor in political science.
Served in the Louisiana State Legislature from 1996 to 2008 before being elected to the U.S. House in 2008.
Served as House Majority Whip (2014–2018) and House Minority Whip (2019–2022) before being elected House Majority Leader for the 118th and 119th Congresses.
Critically wounded at a Congressional baseball practice shooting on June 14, 2017; returned to Congress after his recovery.

priorities.text: Describes himself as focused on fiscal discipline, lower taxes, a robust national defense, strong border security and conservative values.
Says he continues working with President Trump to secure the southern border and reverse Biden administration immigration policies.
Prioritizes American energy production, saying he is fighting to enact a national energy strategy to lower prices and reduce dependence on foreign oil.

positions.summary: Says he continues to work with President Trump to secure the southern border and reverse what his site calls the prior administration's "pro-amnesty policies."
Advocates a national energy strategy that increases production of American oil and gas, describing it as pursuing "American energy dominance" rather than a faster shift away from fossil fuels.
Highlights his role passing the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and describes himself as an advocate for lower taxes.
Site describes him as partnering with federal and state law enforcement to keep communities safe.
Site says he works to "give parents a say in their child's education."

record.text: Led passage of the RESTORE Act, signed into law in 2012, dedicating the majority of Clean Water Act fines from the Deepwater Horizon oil spill to Gulf Coast restoration.
Elected House Majority Leader by House Republicans for the 118th and 119th Congresses (2023–present).

summary.text: Lauren Jewett is a special education teacher in Jefferson Parish running as the Democratic candidate for Louisiana's 1st Congressional District. She previously ran for the Jefferson Parish School Board (2022) and the Louisiana Board of Elementary and Secondary Education (2023).

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Rochester (2009) and a graduate degree from Middlebury College (2023); works as a teacher.

Ran for the Jefferson Parish School Board in 2022 and for the Louisiana Board of Elementary and Secondary Education (BESE) in 2023; endorsed by the Democratic Party of Louisiana in that BESE campaign.

priorities.text: As a career special education teacher, says she is focused on equity for all students, mental health and wellness supports in schools, and educators' working conditions and pay, based on her prior campaign for the state Board of Elementary and Secondary Education.

summary.text: Randall Arrington is a Republican candidate for Louisiana's 1st Congressional District. He previously ran in the 2026 Republican primary for U.S. Senate before withdrawing from that race.
Liddy Glass is an unaffiliated candidate on the ballot for Louisiana's 1st Congressional District.
